b:
I believe that a person's feelings cannot be fully expressed in any language other than their mother tongue. So this post is in Tamil

Six years is a long, long journey. You are forced to sacrifice the greater part of your youth. From a society that hails you as a doctor the moment you enter the medical faculty, you step into a new world of medicines, medicine, and the administration and politics that come with it. Our great bursar hammered in the first nail, saying that to become a doctor you must pass more than 50 exams scoring over 50, and the seniors who came right after hammered in the next nail, saying there were only two weeks of holiday a year, and closed the coffin. Yes. The next few months were the journey of a body that had given up its soul. Language trouble, mental trouble, money trouble, and along with all of that, studying became a trouble in a way I had never seen in 13 years. When Saraswati had to sing me the song "Don't go", I broke. The Kaveri and the Ganges that flowed from it belong to Amma's lap

In my school days I had got used to keeping my circle of friends one circle further out. Though my university circle of friends was large, it was a circle that only shared happiness, so sharing sorrow felt a little awkward. The struggle in my mind finally won, thanks to a few helping hands. In these six years I have found comfort with many. There were very many days when I was a heap of negative feelings: tears, humiliation, disappointment, fear, doubt, confusion, anger, hatred. Lifelong thanks to the few who kept me from falling apart in them

What refined me in study and in mind was the time I spent in the hospital. That I, who cried at the sight of an old woman who had lost herself to age, could face even a death in my own home without falling apart at the end of six years, is the wisdom of the profession. The hospital patients who shared those moments with me are equal to the gods who dwell in the heavens

And if the one who was helpless can do something today, thanks to the teachers who were the reason

Unforgettable thanks, even to those I have forgotten
note: Saraswati is the goddess of learning; the Kaveri and the Ganges stand for tears. "Equal to the gods who dwell in the heavens" is a phrase from Thirukkural 50.
